subject.title: fix(msteams): add timeouts to file consent upload requests

question: Should Microsoft Teams file uploads use the proposed five-minute base plus 256 KiB/s total deadline, with this consent-upload PR landing before the broader SharePoint timeout PR?
rationale: Tests and transport proof establish correctness, but only the Microsoft Teams owner can accept the intentional cutoff for very slow real-tenant transfers and choose the canonical landing order for two branches editing the same helper.

options.title: Approve policy and land consent first
options.body: Accept the transfer budget, land this narrower PR, and require the SharePoint PR to rebase and reuse its shared helper.

options.title: Land SharePoint first
options.body: Accept the policy through the broader SharePoint PR, then rebase this PR onto that canonical helper before landing.

options.title: Recalibrate the deadline
options.body: Pause both PRs until the Teams owner selects a different throughput floor or obtains live-tenant evidence for the proposed cutoff.

recommendation.title: Approve policy and land consent first
recommendation.body: Accept the transfer budget, land this narrower PR, and require the SharePoint PR to rebase and reuse its shared helper.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged history directly covers authorization and lifecycle behavior in the same file-consent path.
